i_can_exact_text: I can distinguish an observation from an inference.
I can distinguish a hypothesis, scientific law, and scientific theory by what each does in science.
I can decide whether a claim is testable and use evidence to judge whether the claim is supported.
I can explain what a formula or model says about the relationship between physical quantities.
I can explain Newton’s First Law in everyday language.
I can explain that inertia is a property of matter, not a force.
I can distinguish between no forces acting and zero net force.
I can identify weight, support force, and applied pushes or pulls acting on an object in a simple situation.
I can use vector arrow direction and length to represent a force’s direction and relative magnitude.
I can combine forces acting in the same or opposite directions to determine net force.
I can determine the direction and relative magnitude of the resultant/net force from a simple force-vector diagram.
I can distinguish static equilibrium from dynamic equilibrium.
I can explain how an object can have forces acting on it and still have zero net force.
I can use the equilibrium rule to determine an unknown horizontal or vertical force.
I can explain why zero net force means an object remains at rest or moves with constant velocity in a straight line.
I can draw a force diagram that includes only the forces acting on the chosen object.
I can use a force diagram to decide whether the forces are balanced or unbalanced.
I can use net force to predict whether an object’s velocity will stay the same or change.
I can critique and revise an incorrect force model or force explanation using evidence and physics vocabulary.
